## 3. Verified source record

The complete JSON entry below is copied from the current local source. Preserve its id, author_id, author_name, day, hour, knowledge_key, timestamp, and exact text. Candidate prose is editorial material, not part of the loaded row.

```json
{
  "id": "journal_raw_b3_43_historian_the_maps",
  "text": "I am cross-referencing the Cartographer's maps with the bunker's existing maps. The Cartographer's maps are more detailed than the fire finder map (exp_report_fire_lookout_01) and cover the areas the bunker has not explored. The fuel and water map shows 2 additional water sources and 1 additional fuel source (a heating oil depot 22km north). The low-dose zone map shows 4 zones within 20km. The settlement map shows 6 settlements within 50km. I am cross-referencing the settlement map with the arrival list (journal_raw_b3_03). 3 of the 6 settlements are unknown to the bunker — the bunker has not encountered them in 225 days. The 3 unknown settlements are the thing the bunker does not know. The not-knowing is the thing the bunker has lived with for 225 days. The not-knowing is the thing the Cartographer's maps reduce. The maps do not remove the not-knowing. The maps reduce it. The reducing is the thing the Historian does. I keep the list of the living. I keep the maps of the known. The living and the known are the things the bunker has. The not-known and the not-living are the things the bunker does not have. The Cartographer's maps move 3 settlements from the not-known to the known. That is the thing the maps do. The maps move things from the not-known to the known. That is the thing the Historian does. I am the Historian. I keep the known. The Cartographer is the thing that expands the known. The Cartographer and the Historian are the same thing in different places. The Cartographer walks the unknown and maps it. The Historian keeps the known and records it. The maps are the thing that connects us. I will cross-reference the maps and I will write the expanded known and I will give it to the council. The known is the thing the bunker has. The known is growing. The growing is the counting up.",
  "timestamp": "Day 226, 14h",
  "author_name": "The Historian",
  "author_id": "the_historian",
  "knowledge_key": "historian_cartographer_maps_cross_reference",
  "day": 226,
  "hour": 14.0
}
```

## 14. Re-reading and variation

Use the passage bank as a set of alternatives. A single approved passage should be edited to fit its source voice and surrounding game text; do not stack all options into one entry. Keep the eight source focuses distinct, vary cadence rather than canon, and retain the original timestamp and knowledge key.

## 15. Cross-content fit

The row belongs to the canonical journal corpus. Adjacent references named by the source may guide a later continuity review, but this plan adds no cross-links, unlock order, or new narrative state. Preserve stated measurements, counts, identities, and chronology exactly until an owner reviews any discrepancy.

## 16. Failure and refusal

Reject any candidate that invents an outcome, motive, conversation, test result, settlement reaction, harvest, treatment effect, or future weather state absent from the row. Reject prose that turns an open question into a puzzle, a person into a lesson, or the source's metaphor into a gameplay rule.

## 17. Replay and callback boundary

All proposed writing is static editorial copy. It requires no random selection, replay state, callback key, persistent memory, or new journal deduplication rule. The source row remains governed by its current catalog and knowledge key.

## 18. Implementation classification

**Classification:** narrative/content proposal only; no code, authored JSON, UI route, save section, feature flag, or runtime integration is included. The local corpus confirms the row and its loader authority, not that this expansion is implemented.

## 19. Acceptance and handoff

- Preserve the complete source JSON row and its exact metadata.
- Select at most one candidate for any future placement; edit it with the content owner.
- Keep chronology, named facts, quantities, uncertainty, and the author's register consistent with the source.
